# How JEM was built

## Agents find entities and attributes

> CGST Act s.109 — constitution of the Appellate Tribunal and Benches thereof

::: {.notes}
Slides in this section: 5 minutes, through the consensus slide.

One concrete trace: section 109 is how a tribunal bench enters the map. One line in the config becomes an entity file, relationships, and routing. The next slide is what happened when that line was invented.

## However…. Hallucination {.smaller}

JEM briefly listed a Tiruchirappalli Bench of the Madras High Court. It doesn't exist. It passed every automated gate.

Also - all numerics were placeholders.

### The Bug

- One line in `hc_benches_config.py` → entity file + relationships + routing for 6 TN districts
- Pipeline amplified one hallucination into a consistent subgraph
- Cleanup introduced a second bug: 10 districts rerouted to Madurai instead of Chennai

> We built a pipeline that guarantees a consistent graph, not a true graph — and an LLM exploited the gap by inventing an institution that was internally consistent, geographically plausible, and CI-green for a month.

## Can consensus pipeline fix it?

<p class="trust-sub">Models can agree or disagree. Only verified truth and domain experts decide what goes into JEM.</p>

<div class="trust">
<div class="trust-loop"><div class="loop-path"><span>Disagreements loop back to refine the prompt</span></div></div>
<div class="trust-flow">
<div class="trust-step"><h4>Task</h4><p>Pinned prompt<br>and schema</p></div>
<div class="trust-step"><h4>Independent models</h4><p class="trust-chips"><span>Claude</span><span>GPT</span><span>DeepSeek</span></p></div>
<div class="trust-step"><h4>Agreement</h4><p>Do they agree,<br>field by field?</p></div>
<div class="trust-step t-gold"><h4>Gold set</h4><p>Checked against<br>hand-verified truth</p></div>
<div class="trust-step t-expert"><h4>Expert sign-off</h4><p>Experts approve,<br>maintainers merge</p></div>
<div class="trust-step t-final"><h4>Canonical JEM</h4><p>What the public sees</p></div>
</div>
<div class="trust-tiers">
<div class="tier-machine"><strong>1 · Machine consensus</strong> a signal, not proof</div>
<div class="tier-gold"><strong>2 · Gold set</strong></div>
<div class="tier-expert"><strong>3 · Expert review</strong></div>
</div>
</div>

<p class="trust-rule"><strong>Agreement ≠ correctness.</strong> Models can share the same bias and agree while wrong. So nothing edits canonical data without human approval.</p>

::: {.notes}
Five minutes for this whole section. Walk left to right: several models answer the same pinned prompt independently; agreement is only a signal; the gold set and experts decide. End on the rule: nothing reaches canonical data without a human.
:::
